question: Should shortcut discovery in WebChat be owned by the existing command inventory/plugin metadata path, by a new first-party `webchat.shortcuts` config surface, or deferred to the broader Control UI plugin contribution-slot design?
rationale: The current product already has slash-command discovery and plugin sidebar tabs, but the requested prompt-snippet panel would add either new core config or new plugin/UI API semantics, and repository direction prefers lean core and plugin-owned optional capability when feasible.

options.title: Use Command Inventory First
options.body: Build the first version as a Control UI browser for existing built-in, skill, and plugin commands, adding prompt insertion only where command metadata can safely express it.

options.title: Approve First-Party Shortcuts Config
options.body: Add a new `webchat.shortcuts` or equivalent config/storage contract with docs, schema, UI, and upgrade tests despite the expanded config surface.

options.title: Wait For Plugin Panels
options.body: Keep this request open until the broader Control UI contribution-slot RFC settles a manifest/plugin panel shape that can host shortcut browsing outside core.

recommendation.title: Use Command Inventory First
recommendation.body: Build the first version as a Control UI browser for existing built-in, skill, and plugin commands, adding prompt insertion only where command metadata can safely express it.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal spans the Control UI command palette/sidebar, chat composer, and plugin tab surfaces implicated by the decision.
